entries.title: Physics Nobel Prize
entries.text: This year, the Physics Nobel Prize went to the IceCube, a telescope made from a cubic kilometer of ice in Antarctica to detect neutrinos, the “ghost particle” nobody has ever seen. Come find out how you build a telescope out of a glacier, what it found, and why Hawaii almost got there first. Join the Physics Club, Thursday 11/12 during lunch in W104.

entries.title: Orchestra Performance
entries.text: Don't miss the Orchestra 4 & 5 performance on Saturday, Nov. 14 at 7 p.m. at the beautiful Moanalua High School Performing Arts Center. Click to purchase tickets ($5) online. We are positive you will enjoy the scintillating sounds of strings presenting music by well-known composers including: Tchaikovsky, Dvraok, Mozart, Paganini, Grainger, and more. This concert features the first of our senior Concerto Competition winners -- Christopher Oyama '27 performing the exciting Violin Concerto by Jean Sibelius, Mvt III -- and also includes musicians from our Band program to create the ‘Iolani Symphony Orchestra.

entries.title: Future Business Leaders of America
entries.text: FBLA is excited to announce our upcoming school conference on Nov 24, with the award ceremony on Nov 25! Students can compete in a variety of events, with overall top scorers receiving a $50 gift card and finalists earning medals and certificates. ALL (you do not need to be in FBLA) interested students are encouraged to register and showcase their skills. Please register using this link by Nov 15: https://forms.gle/CzYHhN7MZPiWEwkw9 Please contact klp2801@iolani.org or ec2801@iolani.org for more information.

entries.title: Human Society's Roaring Night in Paradise Gala
entries.text: Every year, the Hawaiian Humane Society Junior Development Council hosts a gala to raise money for animals in need. This year’s theme is A Roaring Night in Paradise, and we’re inviting 500 teens ages 13–18 to join us for a semi-formal evening filled with a dinner buffet, raffle prizes, games, and a photo booth! The event will be hosted at Alohilani on February 13th from 5-9pm. Purchase your ticket by December 20 and receive a FREE raffle ticket for a chance to win a gift card! A parent consent form is included in the ticket link. Contact Rylie Yamamoto ’27, Chairman of the Hawaiian Humane Society Junior. Jr. Tuxes The Roaring 20s eventbrite.com

entries.title: Food4thought
entries.text: “PRODUCE” A SOLUTION!: Our Lower School grows and harvests food in its gardens, but did you know that you can help grow food in the Upper School, too? To be part of this new initiative, or to volunteer for an upcoming Lower School harvest, contact Ms. Sakuda in the C+CE Office! Be a food producer! GRADES 7-8--FOOD4THOUGHT: STUDENTS AS PRODUCERS!: In the food cycle, you can be part of production, too. Connect with ʻāina and help feed your community! Watch this video (~3:30) for ways you can volunteer with singer Jack Johnsonʻs Kōkua Foundation.
